rationale: Both reviews independently catch the same real numactl-flags-as-server-flags bug and are well-organized with concrete file/line fixes, but Y goes materially deeper: it explicitly flags that Ref2VA was never measured and is a likely OOM risk on the two-GPU profile, which is the closest analog to the ground-truth reviewer's 'have you tested ref2va?' concern, while X only touches this tangentially. Y also surfaces several self-contradictions within the document itself (the memory-model formula contradicting its own 'past eight GPUs' claim, a reference to a nonexistent 'RTX PRO 5000 profile', 1Hz sampling versus a 1.8s VAE-decode window, GDDR7-vs-HBM/96-vs-95.6GiB) that are verifiable from the diff text and arithmetic alone, giving it higher grounded precision density despite covering more ground. X's stage-time-sum discrepancy catch for the 2-GPU config is a nice, precise find, but overall X's issue set is comparatively surface-level (paths, cross-links, template nits) next to Y's structural and quantitative critiques.
